fatal_errors: The proposed material is Q235 carbon steel, whereas the target system is an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L.
The central intervention—grain-boundary tailoring of bare steel—omits atmospheric plasma spraying, the approximately 150 µm HEA coating, and the target 550 °C for 2 h post-coating anneal.
The exposure conditions do not reconstruct either the 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C cyclic molten-salt tests.
No supporting prior evidence is cited for the asserted relationship between annealing, reduced high-angle-boundary fraction, and improved pitting resistance in Q235.

The annealing schedule is unspecified, so the proposed intervention is not reproducible and cannot reliably isolate grain-boundary character from grain size, phases, residual stress, or surface-scale changes.
explanation: The hypothesis is testable in a general sense and appropriately identifies an untreated reference, EBSD characterization, pit-initiation metrics, and restricted environmental boundaries. It also has a weak conceptual overlap with the target because both invoke annealing-induced grain-boundary changes and improved corrosion behavior. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, coating intervention, annealing condition, passive Al/Cr-rich oxide mechanism, or sulfuric-acid and high-temperature molten-salt environments. Its prediction that the benefit will be stronger at 60 °C is unsupported, and annealing bare Q235 can alter grain size, phases, residual stress, surface oxides, and inclusions, preventing attribution to high-angle boundaries without tighter controls. The stated falsification rule also treats the appearance of confounders as falsification rather than as failure of intervention isolation. With no cited evidence and no specified thermal protocol, this is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the reported study.
